answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by weighing each identity by the river of value flowing through it, not by the number of names it holds. Work travels along a trellis of producers and consumers, and an identity gains weight only when independent agents consume its output and stake that it was useful. A lotus floats on the surface and draws nothing from the water, and a fake identity is the same: nothing flows through it, so it weighs nothing. Each fake needs its own real consumers, bought one at a time, so the thousandth fake costs as much as the first and no batch discount exists.
